_comment: Per-service bottleneck model. 'failureMode' decides what happens past saturation: 'throttle' = reject/queue excess but STAY UP (429/503 that recovers); 'offline' = sustained overload exhausts the real resource (CPU / connections) and the service becomes unresponsive; 'none' = traffic source / unbounded. 'offlineAtRatio' is the demand/capacity ratio that, when sustained, flips an 'offline' service down. Engine: simulation.service.ts. Capacity formulas are documented per service in capacityDriver. All 64 services classified.

client.capacityDriver: Request rate you set (or variable-traffic peak)
client.summary: Represents the end users generating traffic. It is the load source for everything downstream — it never bottlenecks or goes offline; its 'capacity' is simply the request rate (or variable-traffic peak) you configure.

route53.summary: Fully managed DNS with effectively unlimited query throughput. Under extreme rates AWS throttles resolutions, but the service stays up — it does not go offline. Bottleneck: request throughput, with a very high ceiling.

cognito.summary: Managed authentication that scales to high sign-in and token rates. Sustained spikes are throttled (TooManyRequests / 429) rather than failing. Bottleneck: request throughput against the user-pool quota.

cloudfront.capacityDriver: Edge request throughput (eased by cache hit rate)
cloudfront.summary: A global edge CDN with massive request capacity. Cache hits are answered at the edge, so only misses reach the origin. It throttles under extreme load but never goes offline. Bottleneck: request throughput, reduced by the cache hit rate.

apiGateway.capacityDriver: Account steady-state RPS limit + integration timeout
apiGateway.summary: A managed front door with an account-level steady-state request limit. Excess requests return 429 (throttled) and the gateway stays up. Bottleneck: request throughput plus the integration timeout.

lambda.summary: Serverless compute bound by concurrent executions, not raw RPS. Effective capacity = concurrency ÷ execution time. Beyond it, requests are throttled (429) while AWS scales out — it does not go offline. Bottleneck: reserved concurrency.

sns.summary: Managed pub/sub with high publish throughput. Excess publishes are throttled rather than failing the service. Bottleneck: publish request throughput.

sqs.summary: Standard queues have effectively unlimited throughput; FIFO queues cap at 300 messages/s (3,000 with batching). Over the limit, sends are throttled — the queue does not go offline. Bottleneck: FIFO throughput cap (standard is practically unbounded).

kinesis.capacityDriver: Shard count (1,000 records/s or 1 MB/s each)
kinesis.summary: Throughput is provisioned in shards — 1,000 records/s (1 MB/s) per shard. Exceeding a shard throttles (ProvisionedThroughputExceeded); you add shards to scale. Bottleneck: shard count.

kinesisFirehose.summary: A buffered delivery stream that auto-scales ingest. Bursts are buffered or throttled, not failed. Bottleneck: ingest throughput governed by the buffer interval and size.

dynamoDb.summary: On-demand mode scales automatically; provisioned mode caps at your RCU/WCU. Over capacity, requests are throttled (ProvisionedThroughputExceeded) while the table stays up. Bottleneck: provisioned read/write capacity units (or per-partition throughput).

s3.summary: Object storage with effectively unlimited request and durability capacity at application scale. It is not an RPS bottleneck and does not go offline. Bottleneck: practically none — per-prefix request rate is extremely high.

cloudWatch.summary: Managed metrics and logs ingestion with very high API limits. Bursts are throttled, never taken offline. Bottleneck: ingestion / API request throughput.

ecs.summary: Containers run on real CPU and memory you provision. Capacity ≈ tasks × vCPU ÷ request time. Sustained overload saturates task CPU, requests time out, and unhealthy tasks are killed — so the service goes OFFLINE until it scales out or load drops. Bottleneck: task CPU (vCPU × task count).

elastiCache.summary: In-memory cache bound by node CPU, memory and client connections. Throughput is very high normally, but sustained overload (or memory pressure and hot keys) exhausts the node — connections time out and it goes OFFLINE. Bottleneck: node count × per-node CPU/connections.

openSearch.summary: A search and analytics cluster bound by data-node CPU and JVM heap. Heavy queries and aggregations saturate the nodes; circuit breakers trip and the cluster returns 5xx / goes OFFLINE. Bottleneck: data-node count × per-node query concurrency.

rds.summary: A relational database bound by its connection pool and per-query CPU/IO. Heavy or slow queries exhaust connections and CPU; new requests get 503s and the instance becomes unresponsive — OFFLINE. Read replicas raise read capacity. Bottleneck: effective parallel queries (cores) ÷ query time.

elb.summary: Managed load balancer that scales capacity automatically; excess connections queue or shed rather than failing. Bottleneck: connection / LCU throughput.

ec2.capacityDriver: vCPU x instance count / request time
ec2.summary: A server you size yourself. Sustained overload saturates CPU and the instance stops responding (offline). Bottleneck: instance CPU - add instances or autoscale.

stepFunctions.summary: Managed orchestration limited by state transitions; bursts are throttled, not failed. Bottleneck: state-transition throughput.

vpc.capacityDriver: Not in the request hot path
vpc.summary: A network boundary, not a request-processing service - it has no throughput bottleneck of its own and never fails under load.

iam.summary: Identity and access control evaluated alongside requests; it is not a traffic bottleneck and does not go offline.

autoScalingGroup.capacityDriver: Instance count between min and max
autoScalingGroup.summary: Manages an EC2 fleet between a min and max size. Capacity grows with instances, but past the max it saturates and backing instances fail (offline). Bottleneck: max instance count.

securityGroup.summary: A virtual firewall applied to traffic - it filters, it does not process load, so it has no capacity bottleneck.

natGateway.summary: Managed NAT with very high bandwidth; extreme connection counts hit port-allocation limits and drop, but it stays up. Bottleneck: bandwidth / port allocations.

batch.summary: Runs jobs on a managed compute pool. Excess work queues rather than failing the service. Bottleneck: compute-environment vCPUs.

eks.summary: Kubernetes on worker nodes you provision. Sustained overload saturates node CPU and pods become unresponsive (offline). Bottleneck: worker-node CPU.

aurora.summary: Cloud-native relational DB bound by its connection pool and per-query CPU; heavy queries exhaust it and return 503s (offline). Replicas add read capacity. Bottleneck: connections x query cost.

eventBridge.summary: Managed event bus with high ingestion limits; bursts are throttled, never offline. Bottleneck: event throughput / rule quotas.

msk.summary: Managed Kafka; producers face backpressure and throttling past broker/partition throughput rather than the service failing. Bottleneck: broker and partition throughput.

waf.summary: Inspects requests at the edge with very high capacity; it throttles rather than failing. Bottleneck: request inspection throughput.

efs.summary: Elastic shared file storage that scales throughput with usage; it is not a request bottleneck and does not go offline.

athena.summary: Serverless SQL over S3; concurrent queries beyond the account quota are queued/throttled, not failed. Bottleneck: concurrent-query limit.

secretsManager.summary: Stores secrets behind a rate-limited API; bursts are throttled. Bottleneck: API request rate - cache secrets to avoid it.

transitGateway.summary: Connects networks at high bandwidth; over the per-attachment limit traffic is shaped, not dropped to offline. Bottleneck: per-attachment bandwidth.

directConnect.summary: A dedicated network link with fixed bandwidth; traffic past the port speed is queued/dropped but the link stays up. Bottleneck: port bandwidth.

globalAccelerator.summary: Routes users over the AWS backbone with very high capacity; it throttles, never goes offline. Bottleneck: edge throughput.

xray.summary: Ingests distributed traces with sampling; excess is sampled/throttled rather than failing. Bottleneck: trace ingestion rate.

redshift.summary: Data warehouse bound by node CPU and concurrency slots; heavy analytical queries saturate the cluster and it stops responding (offline). Bottleneck: node count x query slots.

glue.summary: Serverless ETL on DPUs; extra jobs queue rather than failing the service. Bottleneck: DPU capacity / concurrent-job limit.

emr.summary: Big-data cluster on nodes you size; sustained overload saturates the cluster and tasks fail (offline). Bottleneck: core/task node CPU.

mq.summary: Managed message broker bound by broker connections and CPU; overload exhausts the broker and it becomes unresponsive (offline). Bottleneck: broker connections x throughput.

kms.summary: Key management with a per-region crypto request limit; bursts are throttled - cache data keys to avoid it. Bottleneck: cryptographic request rate.

shield.summary: DDoS protection that mitigates attacks rather than processing your traffic - it has no request-rate bottleneck.

organizations.summary: Account and policy governance - entirely control-plane, never in the request path or a bottleneck.

codePipeline.summary: Orchestrates build/deploy stages - a control-plane workflow, not a runtime traffic bottleneck.

codeBuild.summary: Runs build jobs on managed compute; concurrent builds beyond the limit queue rather than failing. Bottleneck: build concurrency / compute size.

codeDeploy.summary: Coordinates deployments to your compute - a control-plane service with no runtime traffic bottleneck.

bedrock.summary: Managed foundation-model API limited by tokens and requests per minute; over the quota calls are throttled, not failed. Bottleneck: model TPM/RPM quota.

sageMaker.summary: Hosts ML inference on instances you provision; sustained load saturates the endpoint and it stops responding (offline). Bottleneck: endpoint instances - enable autoscaling.

appSync.summary: Managed GraphQL with high request capacity; bursts are throttled, never offline. Bottleneck: request / resolver throughput.

iotCore.summary: Ingests device messages at very high rates; excess is throttled rather than failing. Bottleneck: message ingestion / connection rate.

rekognition.summary: Managed vision API with a per-second request quota; bursts are throttled, not failed. Bottleneck: API request rate.

textract.summary: Managed document-analysis API limited by requests per second; over the quota calls are throttled. Bottleneck: API request rate.

mediaConvert.summary: Transcodes media as jobs that queue when busy rather than failing. Bottleneck: concurrent transcode jobs.

cloudTrail.summary: Records account activity; high event volumes are batched/throttled, never taken offline. Bottleneck: event ingestion rate.

backup.summary: Runs scheduled backups out of the request path - not a runtime bottleneck and never offline.

appRunner.summary: Fully managed containers that autoscale on concurrency; past the max instances requests queue/throttle rather than failing. Bottleneck: max instances x per-instance concurrency.

elasticBeanstalk.summary: Runs your app on managed EC2 instances; sustained overload saturates them and they fail (offline). Bottleneck: instance CPU - scale the environment.

fsx.summary: High-performance shared file storage; throughput is provisioned but it is not a request bottleneck and does not go offline.

certificateManager.summary: Provisions and renews TLS certificates - control-plane only, never a traffic bottleneck.

systemsManager.summary: Operational management and configuration - control-plane, not part of request processing.

ecr.summary: Container image registry; pulls are high-throughput and cached at deploy time, so it is not a runtime request bottleneck.

privateLink.summary: Private connectivity to services with high bandwidth; over the endpoint limit traffic is shaped, not failed. Bottleneck: endpoint bandwidth / connections.
